newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COURT TELLS BELGIAN BANKS TO EXTEND CLABECQ CREDIT.
newsitem.headline: COURT TELLS BELGIAN BANKS TO EXTEND CLABECQ CREDIT.

text.p: Belgian banks have been ordered by court to extend credit lines worth 650 million Belgian francs to bankrupt steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA for two months, Belgian media said on Wednesday.
"Now (the banks) will be forced to reopen their credit lines," a union leader told RTBF radio. The request to reopen the credit lines had been made by the unions.
Banks will appeal the court order. "Naturally we will appeal this decision," Michel Janssens, a lawyer for Generale Bank, told Belgian television BRTN.

Banking industry officials were not reachable for comment, but Michel Tilmant, chief executive officer of Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), indicated at a lunchtime speech on Wednesday that at an extension of credit lines to Clabecq was an unacceptable risk for his bank.

Last week, Belgium's Walloon Region turned down a request by Clabecq's court-appointed receivers for 800 million francs worth of financing for Clabecq, casting doubt on efforts to keep the maker of heavy plate running.
The Walloon government is Clabecq's biggest shareholder and creditor.
